fixes.explanation: This one is true, friend. All Israel comes to David at Hebron and says, "Here we are, your own flesh and blood." (1 Chronicles 11:1) They walk right up and call him family.
A census is counting heads, friend, and that's not what happens at Hebron. The text says David "…made a covenant with them before the LORD." (1 Chronicles 11:3) A covenant is a serious agreement.

Casting lots is a fair guess, friend, but it's not what this verse says. The verse says, "And they anointed him king over Israel…" (1 Chronicles 11:3) So the elders anoint David. That's how he's made king here.
Yes, baker. The anointing happens "…according to the word of the LORD through Samuel." (1 Chronicles 11:3) The LORD's word came through Samuel. The elders are acting in line with it.

This one is true, friend. The verse says they anointed him king "…according to the word of the LORD through Samuel." (1 Chronicles 11:3) The word came through Samuel. So the anointing matches what the LORD had said.
That's what they say, baker. The people of Jebus tell David, "You will never get in here." (1 Chronicles 11:5) Hold onto that line, because the very same verse has an answer for it.

Not quite, baker. The people of Jebus say, "You will never get in here." But the text says, "Nevertheless, David captured the fortress of Zion (that is, the City of David)." (1 Chronicles 11:5) They said never, and the verse says David captured it.

Right, baker. After the people of Jebus say, "You will never get in here." the text says, "Nevertheless, David captured the fortress of Zion (that is, the City of David)." (1 Chronicles 11:5) That "nevertheless" turns the whole scene around. They said never, and the verse says David captured it.

That's not the prize on offer, friend. David says, "Whoever is the first to strike down a Jebusite will become chief commander." (1 Chronicles 11:6) The reward is the top spot as chief commander. No wedding is mentioned here.

Yes, baker. "…Joab son of Zeruiah went up first, and he became the chief." (1 Chronicles 11:6) David put the job on the table, and Joab went up first. Me? I'd have been the one asking who goes second.

Right, baker. "So David took up residence in the fortress; that is why it was called the City of David." (1 Chronicles 11:7) The king moves in and the fortress takes his name. My name's carved on my handle, so I know how good it feels to have your name on something.

City of Palms isn't the name here, friend. The text says, "…David took up residence in the fortress; that is why it was called the City of David." (1 Chronicles 11:7) The name comes from the king who moved in, so the blank is David.

Not this time, baker. In this passage, "…David took up residence in the fortress; that is why it was called the City of David." (1 Chronicles 11:7) The fortress is named for the king who moved in, so the blank is David.

That's right, baker. David "…built up the city around it, from the supporting terraces to the surrounding wall, while Joab restored the rest of the city." (1 Chronicles 11:8) David builds up the city around the fortress, and Joab restores the rest. So each of them has a part in the work.
